# reglobal

> CLI that reinstalls the global npm packages from one Node version into another, for example after `fnm use 26`. Use it when a user has switched or upgraded Node and their global commands are missing, instead of listing and installing them yourself. Run it with `npx reglobal` (preferred: a global install belongs to one Node version, so it is missing after a switch), or `npm install -g reglobal`. Node >= 22, no dependencies.

## Workflow

1. Name the two versions: `reglobal <old> <new>`, for example `reglobal 24.22.3 26.13.1` or `reglobal 24 26`. With only `<old>`, it installs into the Node in use, the one running reglobal (`node --version`).
2. Preview: `reglobal 24 26 --dry-run --json`. Nothing is installed and nothing is asked.
3. Show the user the `plan` and every entry in `warnings`, and get their agreement. Point out each `"majorUpdate": true`: `@latest` is a new major version there, which can break things. Ask which packages to leave out.
4. Install: the same command with `--yes` in place of `--dry-run`, and `--skip a,b` (or `--only a,b`) for what the user left out. Check `installed` and `failed` in the JSON.

Do not pipe `y` into the prompt: use `--yes`. Without `--yes`, with `--json` or with no terminal, reglobal installs nothing and exits 1 (`NEEDS_YES`). `-i` is a checklist for people at a terminal: agents use `--skip` and `--only`.

## Options

- `<old>` or `--from <version|path>`: the old Node version. `24`, `24.1` or `24.1.0` picks the newest installed match (a leading `v` is fine). A path is that version's install folder or its global `node_modules`. Default: the newest installed version other than `<new>`.
- `<new>` or `--to <version|path>`: the Node to install into, matched the same way. Default: the Node in use. For another version, reglobal runs that version's own `node` and the `npm` in its global folder, and sets `npm_config_prefix` to that version's folder (replacing whatever npx passed down), so packages are built for and installed into that Node.
- `--dry-run`: show the plan, install nothing.
- `--yes` (`-y`): install without asking.
- `--keep-versions`: install the versions the old Node had (`typescript@5.4.0`), and git packages at the same commit. Default: `@latest`, and the latest commit.
- `--skip <names>`: leave these out. `--only <names>`: install just these. Comma or space separated, or repeat the option. Each name must be one of the packages to install, or reglobal exits 1 (`BAD_NAME`) and installs nothing. They don't go together.
- `-i`, `--interactive`: a checklist at the terminal (up/down, space, `a` for all or none, enter, `q` to cancel). Not with `--json` or `--yes`.
- `--offline`: don't look up the latest versions. By default, each registry package to install is looked up at `<registry>/<name>/latest` (the registry is `npm_config_registry`, or registry.npmjs.org). Only the package name is sent, never a token. If the lookup fails, `latest` is `null` and there is a warning: not an error.
- `--list`: compare the old version's globals with this one's, read-only. Does not take the install options.

At the prompt (a terminal, no `--yes`), `y` installs, `e` asks for names to leave out and asks again, and anything else cancels (exit 3).
- `--json`: JSON on stdout. npm's own output, and without `--json` the `WARNING:` lines, go to stderr.

Versions are found by reading folders, never by running the old Node or npm: fnm (`FNM_DIR`, or its default folder), nvm (`NVM_DIR`, `~/.nvm`), nvm-windows (`NVM_HOME`), mise (`MISE_DATA_DIR`), asdf (`ASDF_DATA_DIR`, `~/.asdf`) and n (`N_PREFIX`, `/usr/local`). For anything else, pass `--from <path>`. The current Node's globals are in the npm prefix (`npm_config_prefix`), or next to `node`.

Installing is one `npm install --global -- <specs>` run by the current Node with its own npm (`npm-cli.js` next to `node`, or the first on PATH), never through a shell. `REGLOBAL_NPM_CLI=<path to npm-cli.js>` picks another.

## Export and import

For another machine or manager, or when the old version is gone:

- `reglobal export [<file>] [--from <version|path>] [--yes] [--json]` writes the globals of the Node in use (or `--from`) as JSON. With no file, it goes to stdout. An existing file is only overwritten with `--yes`; otherwise it exits 1 with `FILE_EXISTS`. npm, corepack and broken folders are left out, and npm links are kept with `"status": "linked"` and their local path. With `--json` and a file, stdout gets `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "command": "export", "file", "from", "packages": <count> }`.
- `reglobal import <file> [<new>]` (or `--to`) installs from the file with the normal workflow and options above: preview with `--dry-run --json`, then `--yes`. `--list` compares. `--from` does not go with it. In the JSON, `from` is `{ "version", "manager", "dir": null, "file" }`.

The file:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "kind": "reglobal-export",
  "exportedAt": "2026-11-25T18:41:33.678Z",
  "from": { "version": "24.3.0", "manager": "fnm" },
  "packages": [
    { "name": "typescript", "version": "5.4.0", "source": "registry" },
    { "name": "from-git", "version": "1.0.0", "source": "git", "resolved": "git+https://github.com/someone/from-git.git#abc" },
    { "name": "my-tool", "version": "0.1.0", "status": "linked", "link": "/home/me/src/my-tool" }
  ]
}
```

Import treats the file as untrusted. Each `name` must be a valid npm package name, or it exits 1 with `BAD_FILE` and installs nothing. A `version` that isn't plain version text is dropped (it gets `@latest`), and `source` is worked out again from `resolved`, not taken from the file. A file that isn't a reglobal export, isn't JSON, or has a newer `schemaVersion` also exits 1 with `BAD_FILE`.

## JSON

`--list --json`:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "command": "list",
  "from": { "version": "24.3.0", "manager": "fnm", "dir": "/home/me/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/v24.3.0/installation/lib/node_modules" },
  "to": { "version": "26.1.0", "manager": "fnm", "dir":"/home/me/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/v26.1.0/installation/lib/node_modules" },
  "packages": [
    { "name": "typescript", "version": "5.4.0", "source": "registry", "status": "install", "latest": "5.9.3", "majorUpdate": false },
    { "name": "cowsay", "version": "1.6.0", "source": "registry", "status": "present", "currentVersion": "1.7.0" },
    { "name": "npm", "version": "10.0.0", "source": "registry", "status": "skipped", "currentVersion": "11.0.0" },
    { "name": "my-tool", "version": "0.1.0", "status": "linked", "link": "/home/me/src/my-tool" }
  ],
  "summary": { "install": 1, "excluded": 0, "present": 1, "skipped": 1, "linked": 1, "manual": 0, "broken": 0 },
  "warnings": ["my-tool is an npm link to /home/me/src/my-tool: not reinstalled. Run npm link again in that folder."]
}
```

- `latest` and `majorUpdate`: only on registry packages to install, and not with `--offline` or `--keep-versions`. `majorUpdate` is true when `latest` is a newer major version (or, below 1.0, a newer minor).
- `status`: `install` (missing here), `excluded` (left out with `--skip`, `--only`, `e` or the checklist), `present` (already here; `currentVersion` is this one's), `skipped` (npm and corepack come with Node), `linked` (an `npm link`: never installed), `manual` (installed from a local file: install it again by hand), `broken` (no readable package.json).
- `source`: `registry`, `git`, `file` or `url`; anything but `registry` also has `resolved`. Taken from npm's `node_modules/.package-lock.json` or the package's `_resolved`, and `registry` when neither says.
- `from.manager` and `from.version` are `null` when `--from` was a path they can't be read from.

Installing (`--dry-run --json`, `--yes --json`) prints the same fields, with `"command": "install"` and:

```json
{
  "dryRun": false,
  "keepVersions": false,
  "plan": [{ "name": "typescript", "version": "5.4.0", "source": "registry", "spec": "typescript@latest", "latest": "5.9.3", "majorUpdate": false }],
  "npmExitCode": 0,
  "installed": ["typescript"],
  "failed": []
}
```

`npmExitCode`, `installed` and `failed` are only there after npm ran. A package counts as installed when its folder is in this Node's globals afterwards. On failure the same object also has `error`.

Errors, with `--json`, are on stdout: `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "error": { "code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": "..." } }`. Codes: `NO_OLD_VERSION`, `NOT_FOUND`, `BAD_VERSION`, `BAD_NAME`, `BAD_FILE`, `FILE_EXISTS`, `NEEDS_YES`, `NEEDS_TERMINAL`, `NO_NODE`, `NO_NPM`, `INSTALL_FAILED`, `UNKNOWN_OPTION`, `UNKNOWN_COMMAND`, `BAD_OPTION`.

## Exit codes

- `0`: installed everything in the plan, or a dry run or list was shown.
- `1`: error: no old version, a bad name in `--skip`/`--only`, npm failed or left a package out, or `--yes` was needed.
- `2`: nothing to install (also from `--dry-run`, or when `--skip` left nothing): not an error.
- `3`: cancelled at the prompt or the checklist, or nothing was left ticked.
